mechanisms.behavior: Five balls occupy switches 17-21, including one ceramic white ball identified through dedicated public switch 71. Output 1 advances the rightmost ball through jam opto 22 toward shooter-lane switches 23/50.
mechanisms.label: Five-ball trough with ceramic ball

mechanisms.behavior: Output 2 fires the auto plunger while the cabinet manual plunger remains functional. The Limited Edition adds top shooter-lane switch 50; Standard uses switch 23 only.
mechanisms.label: Auto launcher and manual plunger

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 53 senses the bottom of the center lock and switch 46 the upper left-lock position. Output 3 raises the lock, while output 4 energizes the latch; when the latch releases, the two lock barriers drop together to release the held ball route.
mechanisms.label: Center lock lift and latch

mechanisms.behavior: Outputs 18/19 move the target left/right across seven sensed stops. The proven table clamps travel to -27..+36 degrees: position 1/home at +34..36, 2 at +24..26, 3 at +14..16, 4 at +3..5, 5/park at -7..-6, 6 at -17..-15, and 7/away at -27..-25. All positions share dedicated hit switch 72; switches 33-39 report carriage position and must not fire on target impact. Lamps exist for positions 1-4 and 6-7 but not position 5.
mechanisms.label: Seven-position Moving Mick target

positions.description: +34 through +36 degrees in the proven VPX model
positions.label: Position 1 / home / right

mechanisms.behavior: Output 6 opens and closes the left control gate; there is no endpoint switch.
mechanisms.label: Left controlled gate

mechanisms.behavior: Outputs 15/16 drive the lower left/right flippers. Public button/EOS pairs are 84/83 and 82/81, with normally-closed EOS contacts. The machine has no upper flippers.
mechanisms.label: Two-flipper assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Left, right, and bottom pop output/switch pairs are 9/30, 10/31, and 11/32; lamps 60-62 are their LEDs and output 26 is their shared feature flasher.
mechanisms.label: Three pop bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left and right slings use output/switch pairs 13/26 and 14/27.
mechanisms.label: Two slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Switches 42/45 are the ramp exits, 44/48 the left/right orbits, 41 the passive left-orbit spinner, 43 the pop lane, and 6-9 the four band-member top lanes. The service location diagrams are authoritative for the unswitched ramp entrances and return geometry.
mechanisms.label: Ramps, orbits, spinner, and lanes

mechanisms.behavior: Mick bank switches are 1-3, the right bank is 10-12, STAR standups are 51/57/56, and ROCK STAR standups are 54/55. These are fixed standups, not resettable drop targets.
mechanisms.label: Target banks and standups

mechanisms.behavior: Output 8 is the optional 16 VAC shaker installation and may be absent from a stock machine.
mechanisms.label: Optional shaker motor

mechanisms.behavior: The fuller playfield adds two 50 V magnets and three 20 V up/down posts: outputs 5/7 energize the left/right magnets and 17/30/32 raise the left/center/right posts. Raised posts physically block and kick the ball upward in the proven table. Cabinet buttons D13/D15 serialize as public 88/86 for the side posts; the center post is ROM-driven and has no dedicated player button. Public 87/85 are VPX compatibility states mirrored from the flipper keys and are not separate physical switches. Recreate the five physical actuators, button causality, and ball interaction rather than treating the effect as lamp animation.
mechanisms.label: Premium/LE magnetized ball diverter

mechanisms.behavior: One of the five balls is nonmagnetic ceramic. The proven script preserves its identity through drain/trough recreation, initializes detector 71 active, drives 71 inactive when that ball reaches trough switch 21, and restores it after shooter switch 23 clears. Preserve per-ball identity so magnet behavior and ROM recognition remain coherent.
mechanisms.label: Ceramic white-ball tracking
